chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abul-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated that Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated that Tamim ibn Buhlool, from his father, from Ubaydullah ibn al-Fazl al-Hashemi, said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:
Three are those with whom if one is antagonistic, they will be debased: the father, the ruler, and the creditor.

key_terms.السُّلْطَانُ: the ruler, king, or governing authority
key_terms.الْغَرِيمُ: the creditor, one to whom a debt is owed
key_terms.عَازَهُمْ: to be antagonistic or hostile towards them

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people with whom antagonism leads to humiliation according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), highlighting the socio-religious dynamics of dignity (izzah) versus debasement (dhell). The triad of father, ruler, and creditor reflects the pillars of familial, political, and economic stability in early Shia society, where antagonizing any of these authority figures could lead to social ostracization or loss of status.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-271 Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abul-Ab’bas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qat’tan quoted Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn al-Fazl al-Hashemi that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,
“Whoever is antagonistic with the following three people will be debased: his father, the King and the one who has given him a loan.”
